subject: Edge corridor enablement: initial prerequisites & gating checklist
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood-inference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@lumacare.health>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: InfraSec Team <netsec@lumacare.health>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edge corridor enablement: initial prerequisites & gating checklist

Hi Samir / Lumacare infra team —

As we get ready to enable the private deployment "edge corridor" for your account, I put together an initial gating checklist to make the first validation window as productive as possible. Please review and flag anything we should add or reprioritize.

Top-level asks (high level):
- Provide the canonical VPC/Network owners and service account contact for peering and IAM (name + email).
- Confirm CIDR ranges for the tenant VPCs (primary/secondary) and whether NATed egress is acceptable.
- Confirm preferred connectivity method: VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or PrivateLink (include project constraints).
- Share an allowlist for outbound egress to our control/metrics endpoints (list of FQDNs will follow).
- Provide a point of contact for KMS/HSM access or an explanation of key management constraints.
- SOC 2 evidence request: provide the SOC 2 Type II attestation PDF or point us to your vendor portal.

Technical prerequisites (detailed):
- Subnet layout for the environment (subnet names, AZs, CIDRs) and gateway IPs.
- Proposed BGP session parameters if using a gateway (ASN, MD5, local-pref hints).
- Firewall rules: allow inbound TCP 443 from our peered network to private endpoints (we'll enumerate service ports in follow-up).
- Service account with these minimum roles: ComputeAdmin, NetworkAdmin, KMSDecrypt for the tenancy service account (or equivalent RBAC perms).
- DNS plan: will you provide private hosted zone or should we create split-horizon entries?
- NTP and MTU expectations for VNIs; standard MTU mismatch has caused issues in previous integrations.

Operational & cutover plan:
- A 4-hour net-validation window (preferred PST morning) to run peering, route validation, and small-scale smoke tests.
- A separate maintenance window for final deployment and traffic cutover.
- Backout plan: snapshot schedule and rollback tag to revert to baseline if anomalies observed.

Attachments: network-diagram-v2.pdf (attached), SOW draft (sow-draft-lumacare.docx) — both attached for reference.

Can you confirm the items above and propose the earliest 4-hour validation window (timezone: PST) you can support?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
-- Attachment: network-diagram-v2.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
-- Attachment: sow-draft-lumacare.docx (DOCX, 56KB)

From: Samir Patel <samir@lumacare.health>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: InfraSec Team <netsec@lumacare.health>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge corridor enablement: initial prerequisites & gating checklist

Karthik — thanks for the thorough list. I did a quick pass with our infra and sec leads, and we can comply with most items but need to flag a couple of constraints:

1) KMS/HSM: we use a customer-managed KMS in our Azure subscription and will not share key material. We can create an RBAC identity that allows decrypt to the service account; full key export is not possible.
2) SOC2: our SOC 2 Type II is available but currently behind our vendor portal. I will get InfraSec to generate a redacted copy and link it to you by EOD Monday.
3) Connectivity: we prefer PrivateLink for the control-plane endpoints and Transit Gateway peering for the data plane. We will open a ticket (LUMA-237) in our Jira to track the peering config.

Earliest validation window: Mon 20 Sep 2027, 09:00-13:00 PST. Can Marissa and Ben be available for the first half (09:00-11:00) for peering + route checks? InfraSec will join the second half for firewall and SOC evidence review.

Action items from our side:
- I'll assign the ticket LUMA-237 with network topology and ASN details by COB today.
- InfraSec will upload redacted SOC2 by Monday.

Samir
Operations Lead, Lumacare Health
-- Note: forwarding SSO contact to NetSec in separate mail.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood-inference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@lumacare.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood-inference.com>, InfraSec Team <netsec@lumacare.health>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 07:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge corridor enablement: initial prerequisites & gating checklist

Thanks Samir — that's great and aligns with what I expected. A few clarifications and internal assignments so we're all aligned for Monday: 

- Marissa: please take point on the peering validation and route verification during 09:00-11:00 PST. Confirm the runbook steps you'll execute and post them to the ticket (LUMA-237).
- Ben: lead the smoke tests and firewall rule verification 10:30-12:00 PST, then join InfraSec for SOC artifact review at 12:00 PST.
- Samir / InfraSec: we'll need the redacted SOC2 and the Jira ticket URL before the session so we can attach relevant test evidence.

Runbook highlights for Monday's window (expected):
1) Establish peering / PrivateLink endpoints and confirm route table propagation.
2) Validate NAT/eProxy egress to our metrics/control endpoints (we will test HTTPS POST to our ingest endpoints).
3) Verify TLS cert validation for private endpoints (bring CA chains if custom).
4) Run a limited inference smoke test (10 concurrent streams) to exercise KV cache behavior and observe latencies.

If anyone has blockers to the times above, flag now — otherwise we'll proceed and I will book the validation Zoom and shared logs workspace.

Karthik
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood-inference.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Sep 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge corridor enablement: initial prerequisites & gating checklist

All set from my end. I've attached a short smoke-test runbook and a checklist for the metrics egress validation. High-level test plan attached:

- Connectivity: TCP/443 + TLS handshake verification to private endpoints.
- Authentication: service account JWT exchange and KMS decrypt flow (with RBAC token).
- Inference smoke: 10 concurrent sessions for 15 minutes, capture p50/p95 latencies and error rates.
- Post-test: collect agent logs, KV-cache hit ratio, and a small sample of transcripts for quality verification.

I'll upload the test results artifact to the shared Drive link and link it in LUMA-237 after the window. If InfraSec needs anything additional for the SOC artifacts, ping me.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
